To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kinetic spherical model is exactly solvable, the dynamical exponent is z = 4 and the results agree with those of local scale in variance.

the kinetic spherical model exhibits local scale invariances with z = 4, that the scaling functions for the two-time correlation and the response functions are identical, that the scaling function for the correlation function is a universal function, and that the scaling function of the response function is not universal.

the scaling functions of the two-time correlation and of the two-time response functions of the spherical model can be expressed in terms of the scaling functions of a single time correlation and response function of a reduced deterministic equation, and that these scaling functions can be expressed in closed form as a single integral.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new dynamical symmetry of the stochastic dynamics of the spherical model with conserved order parameter, which we refer to as local scale invariances.
a dynamical system with local scale symmetry.
the kinetics of phase separation in critical systems and the dynamical symmetries of the stochastic differential equation which governs the evolution of such systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local scale invarianc e is the exact symmetry of the critical spherical model.
the local scale invariances of the deterministic part of the stochastic Langevin equation are the exact dynamical symmetries of the full stochastic equation.
the spherical model with conserved order parameter is the only model which can be solved exactly for all times, including the time evolution of the two-point correlation function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the scaling forms for the two-time correlation and the response function of the kinetic spherical model, as obtained from the exact solution, are in agreement with the scaling forms of local scale in variance, with z = 4.
the scaling functions for the two-time correlation and the response functions are identical to those of the Mullins– Herring equation, but with a different time scale.
the scaling forms of the two-time functions in the critical spherical and in the Mullins– Herring model are given by the same scaling functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local scale symmetry of the deterministic part of the Langevin equation, together with a reduction formula, is sufficient to predict scaling forms for the correlation and response functions.

, in addition to the usual scale symmetry of the deterministic part of a Langevin equation, there is also a dynamical symmetry of the stochastic Langevin equation which can be exploited to obtain scaling forms and scaling exponents.
local scale invariances can be used as a guiding principle for the construction of effective theories in non-equilibrium systems.
